source.title: Perturbation Probing: A Two-Pass-per-Prompt Diagnostic for FFN Behavioral Circuits in Aligned LLMs
source.authors: Hong-Liang Liu; Tung-Ling Li; Yuhao Wu

record.tranche_reason: The paper reports causal interventions on FFN neurons and discusses mechanistic interpretability, but it does not test whether neurons have one nameable main job, evaluate neuron explanations on held-out activations, or build the attribution graphs named in the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper's ablations and behavioral circuit results concern neuron-level causal control, not semantic single-job explanations or their predictive accuracy. Appendix M reports overlap among task-defined circuits; that is a related but different measure, recorded under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: The paper ranks FFN neurons by a signed perturbation score and validates them causally for behavioural circuits. It does not label neurons with semantic jobs, does not audit the share of interpretable neurons, does not score explanations by simulated activations, does not study vision neurons, and does not build attribution graphs. It cites Bills et al. only as correlational related work. None of its results bear on V1–V7.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that perturbation probing finds causal FFN neurons for opposition circuits (safety template, sycophancy), where RLHF opposes pre-training. Routing behaviours such as language selection are attention-mediated and respond only to direction injection, under limited conditions. The FFN/Skip ratio predicts which regime applies. The SmolLM3 shared-neuron point is an appendix detail, not a main conclusion.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses perturbation-based neuron ranking followed by ablation, patching, restoration, and direction injection; it does not use the neuron-explanation audit or attribution-graph methods named in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: Causal effectiveness varies with circuit, model architecture, FFN/Skip ratio, perturbation, and behavioral observable.

fits_no_version.finding: In SmolLM3-3B, 22% of neuron slots are shared across sycophancy, tool-use and code-generation circuits, and seven neurons serve all three. Ablating all 26 shared neurons has zero effect on any behaviour.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Neurons shared across task-defined circuits can be causally peripheral, while circuit-specific neurons carry the behavioural effect.

fits_no_version.finding: Behavioural control by small sets of late-layer FFN neurons (for example ~50 of 350,208 for the refusal template in Qwen3-4B) appears only where RLHF opposes pre-training. Other behaviours show readout neurons with no ablation effect.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Causally concentrated FFN neuron circuits exist for opposition behaviours, and their concentration is predicted by the FFN/Skip ratio.

record.problems: The paper does not test the claim versions' semantic explanation measures. Its overlap result concerns task-defined circuits and cannot establish whether neuron poles have one nameable job. Some reported circuit tests also use small prompt sets, as stated in the paper.
record.rows_left_out: Not applicable; no claim-version test results were identified. The recorded rows cover the related circuit-overlap result in Appendix M.

untested.parts: Share of Qwen3-32B neuron poles with one job, two related jobs or unexplained. Qwen3-32B appears only in a direction-injection table.
Interpretable-neuron shares across models and scales.
Reinterpretation of classic vision polysemantic neurons.
Effect of architecture, regularization and tools on the interpretable share.
Neuron-based attribution graphs without a replacement model.

record.verdict_notes: The record's relation and tranche (discusses/T6) are kept. The paper concerns causal localization of behaviour, not neuron interpretability shares or explanation quality. No verdicts are given.

versions.untested_parts: The share of neuron poles with one job, two related jobs, or unexplained jobs in Qwen3-32B.
Interpretable-neuron shares across models, architectures, and scales up to trillions of parameters.
Whether classic vision-model neurons detect coherent shared features or reflect recursive generalization rather than superposition.
Whether architecture, regularization, and tools explain changes in interpretable-neuron share, including the stated InceptionV1-sized estimates.
The paper does not build attribution graphs or report their behavioral explanation quality or reconstruction error.
Whether explanations fitted to activating examples fail to predict where neurons fire.
Automated scoring of neuron explanations by simulating activations on new text.

rows.subject: SmolLM3-3B
rows.operation_detail: Measured neuron-slot overlap among sycophancy, tool-use, and code-generation circuits.
rows.measure: Neuron slots shared across the three circuits
rows.note: Circuit overlap is not a measure of whether neuron explanations name one semantic job or predict activations.
rows.check: Measures overlap among task-defined circuit neuron sets, not whether neurons have one nameable job. The paper calls it 'circuit superposition', which is a different construct from neuron-level polysemanticity in V1/V3.
